definitions.explanation: Money paid regularly to an employee for their work.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}は{毎月|まいつき}25{日|にち}に{出|で}ます。
examples.english: Salary is paid on the 25th of every month.

examples.japanese: {今月|こんげつ}から{給料|きゅうりょう}が{少|すこ}し{上|あ}がりました。
examples.english: My salary went up a little starting this month.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}だけでは{生活|せいかつ}が{大変|たいへん}なので、アルバイトもしています。
examples.english: I can't get by on just my salary, so I also work a part-time job.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}から{税金|ぜいきん}や{保険|ほけん}が{引|ひ}かれるので、{手取|てど}りは{思|おも}ったより{少|すく}ないです。
examples.english: Taxes and insurance are deducted from the salary, so the take-home pay is less than expected.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}して{給料|きゅうりょう}は{少|すこ}し{下|さ}がりましたが、{毎日|まいにち}{定時|ていじ}に{帰|かえ}れるようになったので、{生活|せいかつ}は{前|まえ}より{楽|らく}になりました。
examples.english: My salary dropped a little when I changed jobs, but now I can leave on time every day, so life has become easier than before.

notes:
{給料|きゅうりょう} is the general term for salary or wages paid to employees.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {給料|きゅうりょう}をもらう: to receive a salary
- {給料|きゅうりょう}が{上|あ}がる: salary goes up
- {給料|きゅうりょう}が{下|さ}がる: salary goes down
- {給料|きゅうりょう}から{引|ひ}かれる: to be deducted from salary

RELATED TERMS:
- {月給|げっきゅう}: monthly salary
- {年収|ねんしゅう}: annual income
- {時給|じきゅう}: hourly wage
- {給料日|きゅうりょうび}: payday
- {手取|てど}り: take-home pay (after deductions)
- {額面|がくめん}: gross salary (before deductions)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, many companies pay salaries on the 25th of each month. The expression {給料日前|きゅうりょうびまえ} (before payday) often implies being short on money.
